messages:
Alex Kim: Quick sync — proposal to move RBAC enforcement from the console gateway down into the query multiplexer/runtime. Goal: remove an extra RPC per request and shave ~20-25ms p95 for guarded dashboards. Thoughts?
Priya Nair: Why not just add more caching at the gateway? we already have a permissions cache there, TTLs are easy to tune.
Noah West: Caching helps but we still do a validation RPC to the auth service for cache misses. If we push enforcement deeper we can avoid forwarding user tokens for some read-only paths.
Jess Rivera: Risk: moving checks deeper increases blast radius for any logic bugs in the query layer. Also impacts multi-tenant isolation testing.
Alex Kim: Agreed on risk. Thinking hybrid: shallow allowlist/filter at gateway (fast path), deep RBAC in query for authoritative decision. That lets dashboards that only need broad visibility avoid the extra roundtrip while still letting sensitive routes get full checks.
Priya Nair: Hybrid sounds OK. Need to be explicit about cache invariants so we don't serve stale rows to users who lost access. TTL alone won't cut it for role revocation.
Noah West: We can address revocation with a short TTL + event-driven invalidation. Query layer can accept a capability token for critical reads that bypasses cache and forces authoritative check.
Alex Kim: Example config I sketched for the mux:
```
rbac:
  mode: hybrid
  gateway_shallow_check: true
  capability_token_header: X-Cap-Token
  gateway_cache_ttl: 15s
  revoke_invalidation_topic: console-rbac-invalidations
```
Priya Nair: +1 on capability token. But who mints it? gateway needs to mint scoped tokens for routes it deems safe. That implies gateway has to be trusted and audited.
Jess Rivera: We also need observability hooks: metric for "authorization_stale_serves", counters for capability-token use, histograms for auth latency both at gateway and query.
Noah West: Perf-wise, this should cut p95 on dashboards that currently do per-widget auth RPCs. But cost: added complexity in mux and more token ops. We should quantify unit cost.
Alex Kim: Proposal for rollout:
1) Implement shallow allowlist at gateway + mint capability tokens for low-sensitivity routes.
2) Add deep-check path in query mux that consumes capability tokens and verifies signature + scope.
3) Canary 10% traffic for non-sensitive dashboards, monitor auth-latency, error-rate, and auth-consistency metrics.
4) Expand to 50% with automatic fallback to gateway checks on mismatch for 24h.
5) Full cutover only after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
Priya Nair: Add revocation test cases to the canary: simulate role removal and ensure invalidation topic clears capability tokens quickly. Also add a test harness to replay event ordering.
Jess Rivera: I'll add dashboards: auth.latency.gateway, auth.latency.query_mux, auth.failures.by_route, capability_token.usage, authorization_stale_serves. Plus SLO alarms if p50 gateway auth > 40ms or query_mux auth > 20ms.
Noah West: One more tradeoff: RBAC logic duplication. We'll need a small shared library (policy encoding) used by gateway and mux to avoid divergence. Consider publishing as an internal npm/pypi package.
Alex Kim: Good call. Action items: Priya to draft token minting/security model, Noah to sketch mux verification API + proto, Jess to build monitoring dashboards, I'll put together the canary playbook and tests.
Priya Nair: I'll also run a quick perf sim (qps mix + permission-hit-rate) to estimate token ops cost.
deploy-bot: Deployed branch alex/rbac-hybrid to staging (build #4821) :white_check_mark:
Noah West: Nice. Once staging smoke passes let's schedule a 30m sync to walk through the playbook before canary.
Alex Kim: Thanks all — schedule invite for tomorrow. :thumbsup:
